title: Probabilistic Burst Savings Playbook
content:
Purpose
---
This memo documents a lightweight benchmark & collateral draft for a probabilistic burst-smoothing approach aimed at reducing per-token cost during spiky session workloads while preserving tail latency for interactive applications. The intent is to produce a practical playbook the Optimize/product team can use to evaluate tradeoffs vs. existing prewarm/windowed strategies and to feed into runtime feature proposals.

Context & motivation
---
Observed problem: spikes in short-lived interactive sessions (chat-like) cause frequent cold starts or small batches that increase per-token cost and push p95/p99 latency for interactive tiers. Fully keeping capacity warm is expensive; deterministic prewarm windows add cost and complexity. We explored a low-friction probabilistic admission/prefetch heuristic that smooths bursts by prefetching KV prefixes or warming a small fraction of slots based on recent session arrival statistics.

What we benchmarked
---
Configs (tested on identical hardware/model):
1) Baseline (on-demand): no prewarm, cold slot penalty applied when a new session arrives.
2) Windowed prewarm (fixed): keep X slots warm for Y seconds after last activity (standard prewarm window).
3) Probabilistic smoothing (proposed): after a session ends, the controller keeps a small probability p of retaining a warm slot for the next T seconds; probability is dynamically scaled by recent arrival rate (EWMA).

Workload shape: synthetic sessionized trace derived from production sample (mixed short/long sessions, median session length 18s, 60% sessions < 10s). We introduce synthetic microbursts (10x arrivals for 3s) interspersed with baseline.

Primary metrics:
- latency p50/p90/p95/p99 (ms)
- amortized cost normalized to "$ per 1000 requests" (approx dollars equivalent based on reserved GPU-minute unit cost)
- cold-start fraction (% of sessions encountering >50ms startup penalty)

Benchmark table (aggregated over 24-hour simulated trace)
---
ASCII table:

Config                     | p50  | p90  | p95  | p99  | cold% | $/1000 reqs
---------------------------+------+------+------+------+-------+-----------
Baseline (on-demand)        | 42ms | 128ms| 190ms| 420ms| 21.7% | $10.3
Windowed prewarm (fixed)   | 39ms | 95ms | 120ms| 230ms| 6.1%  | $15.8
Probabilistic smoothing    | 40ms | 82ms | 101ms| 210ms| 7.8%  | $12.9

Notes on table: cost includes amortized warm slot minutes and extra KV cache occupancy. Baseline has lowest unit cost for sustained traffic but poor tail latency during bursts; windowed prewarm reduces tails at material cost. Probabilistic smoothing recovers most of the tail latency benefits while curbing the cost increase.

Percentile band text-chart (p95 to p99 delta from baseline):
- baseline: p95 -> +0ms (ref), p99 -> +230ms
- windowed: p95 -> -70ms, p99 -> -190ms
- probabilistic: p95 -> -89ms, p99 -> -210ms

Breakdown by burst vs steady periods
---
We sliced the trace into Burst windows (3s microbursts) and Steady windows. Results:
- During bursts, probabilistic smoothing delivered p95 close to windowed prewarm but with 20-25% lower warm-minute cost.
- During steady periods, probabilistic falls back to on-demand most of the time, achieving cost close to baseline (within 5–10%).

Operational behavior & sensitivity
---
Key knobs: initial p0, decay half-life for EWMA, max warm slots per node, and T (retention time).
Sensitivity observations from parameter sweep:
- Increasing p0 from 0.05 -> 0.2 reduces cold% linearly but increases cost nonlinearly as cache fragmentation rises.
- Short T (<8s) misses follow-on requests in many sessions; recommended T in experiments = 12–30s depending on median session gap.
- Capping warm slots per node is crucial to avoid tail-heavy slot hoarding when many sessions become active simultaneously.

Micro-observations (raw traces)
---
- Many cold events in baseline are caused by back-to-back short sessions from the same session-id pattern — KV-prefetch makes outsized impact.
- For multimodal token-length workloads, probabilistic strategy favors short-session ROC improvement (p95 down) but provides less improvement for very long generations (these remain bound by model compute).

Cost analysis model (text)
---
We modeled cost as: unit_cost = base_compute + warm_minute_penalty * warm_minutes + cache_memory_penalty. Warm_minutes is number of active warm slots * retention_time aggregated over the trace. Probabilistic approach reduces expected warm_minutes by making retention stochastic and conditioned on arrival intensity. Numerically, in this trace:
- baseline warm_minutes ≈ 12 min per 1000 reqs (only on-demand micro-alloc overhead)
- windowed warm_minutes ≈ 28 min per 1000 reqs
- probabilistic warm_minutes ≈ 18 min per 1000 reqs

Qualitative recommendations
---
- For interactive tiers where p99 > 200ms is visible to users, adopt probabilistic smoothing as a low-cost intermediate between on-demand and heavy prewarm. The UX/cost sweet spot is often p0=0.08, T=18s, decay half-life = 9s for traces like this.
- Expose a per-customer "burst-sensitivity" profile: high-sensitivity (strict tails) -> larger p0 or hybrid (windowed for top N slots), cost-sensitive -> low p0 and longer decay.
- For Dedicated customers who pay for reserved capacity, probabilistic smoothing can be an opt-in runtime flag that reduces RU consumption on bursty multi-tenant machines.

Implementation notes for runtime team
---
- Keep admission decision stateless for the hot path: use a compact EWMA counter and RNG to decide retention; use token-bucket to avoid stampeding the kernel.
- Instrument metrics: retention-decisions, warm-minutes-by-tenant, cold-event-reason, and p95/p99 per retention cohort.
- Add a canary rollout that compares baseline/windowed/probabilistic at 1% tenant traffic to verify conversational UX impacts.

Open questions & next steps
---
- How does probabilistic smoothing interact with model quantization (smaller KV sizes) and with multi-model co-location? Need a cross-benchmark.
- Investigate hybrid heuristics: deterministic prewarm for a tiny hot slot pool + probabilistic for the rest. We sketched this in a small ablation but haven't stress-tested it at scale.
- Consider backed-off prefetch of only KV prefix (not full model warm) as a cheaper variant — requires runtime support to prefetch light-weight state.

Appendix: short-run ablation (numbers from 30 min experiment)
---
Ablation: p0=0.05 v p0=0.12 (T=18s)
- p0=0.05: p95 105ms, p99 215ms, $/1000 11.9
- p0=0.12: p95 98ms, p99 198ms, $/1000 13.6

Action items
---
- Product: confirm target tenant cohorts for a 1% canary. (Asha)
- Runtime: prototype lightweight EWMA + retention decision and add metrics. (Jonah)
- Benchmarking: run cross-model sweep (Llama-2-13B, RedR-7B) and report differences. (Marco)

This is a draft meant for internal review. Feedback sought on the recommended defaults and on how aggressive we should be exposing knobs to customers vs keeping conservative safe defaults.
